//: Type-checking project for CI. It exists because the repository-level tsconfig.json
deliberately still includes examples/**, which do not yet have React types installed
This project type-checks every package, including the *.test.ts files, so type-level
contracts in packages/core are actually gated rather than merely written down.
The two `resolve.alias` fixtures (#97) are excluded, and the reason is the rule they
exist to test rather than an inconvenience: their Cell entries import `@app/shared/thing`,
an id only a bundler holding the project's `alias` can resolve. Type-checking them would
require re-declaring that alias as a tsconfig `paths` entry — a second declaration of one
project's alias set, free to drift from the one the build and the dev server read, which
is exactly what #97 forbids. The fixtures are still exercised: both packages' tests compile
and resolve them through the real alias, which is the stronger check.
